stage1.impression: A warm, coherent night room with a real sense of depth: the fir ceiling, the record wall and the pools under the pendants carry it, and the hung smoked globe gives it a centrepiece no catalogue bar has. But it reads as CG at once: the figures are translucent grey mannequins smeared across the frame, the zinc counter and foreground floor are the brightest surfaces in the frame and read as white plastic and polished grey vinyl, the globe reads as a black wire cage rather than cast acrylic, and the hero speakers at the far end are small white boxes with blown batts in black niches, with no tint and no light through the acrylic. As it stands a magazine would see a generic, well-lit render of a bar, not a specific place, though the globe and record wall hint that it could become one.

blocking_9: Figures must read as clothed people with texture (fabric, hair, skin variation) and only partial motion blur; now they are untextured translucent mannequins (regions [0,300,480,480], [780,380,960,600])

The altar pair must read as the hero at a glance: smoked tinted cabinet visible, edges glowing, batts not clipped; region [505,335,585,435] and [640,335,700,435] lum_median >= 45 with lum_p95 <= 225 (now 29/35 and 233/221)
Mother EARF must read as thick smoked cast acrylic with lit polished edges and see-through depth, not a black wire cage; region [610,0,880,280] lum_median 16-30 and lum_p95 >= 70 (now 9.3 and 42)
The counter top and foreground floor must not be the brightest surfaces: [0,400,340,470] lum_median <= 115 (now 156), [150,560,650,800] lum_median <= 40 (now 51)
The big frames on the right wall must show an image, not blank grey-lilac panels
Visible sign of real materials at 1:1 on the concrete floor and the zinc (patina, wear), no flat CG gradients
Seat and table models repeat identically down the room; needs variation in wear or placement so it reads lived-in

defects.what: counter figures are translucent grey ghosts with no clothing or skin texture; the blur reads as a CG shutter trick, not a quarter-second exposure
banquette figures blurred into smooth grey shapes, faces featureless mannequins
altar speakers: white batts clip (p95 233), cabinets lost in black niches, no visible smoke tint or glowing acrylic edges; the hero is unreadable
Mother EARF reads as an opaque black wire sphere (median 9.3), no glow on its 25 mm edges, no transparency
the globe's 'shadow' on the wall reads as bright light streaks, not a shadow; confusing patch of light on the concrete
zinc counter top reads as white marble/plastic, median 156, brightest large surface in the frame
foreground floor is bright, smooth and grey (median 51, p95 191) with hard stool shadows; reads as polished vinyl and pulls the eye to empty floor
large frame shows a blank grey-lilac field; reads as unrendered texture
back-bar speaker reads as a flat light-grey box (median 130), no tint
identical stools and tables repeated down the room
fir ceiling is good but slightly orange-saturated (r 60, g 32, b 19), competing with the one-colour rule

changes.problem: The hero pair at the altar is unreadable: batts clip while the smoked cabinets disappear into the black niche.

evidence.measured: lum_median 29.1, p95 232.9, clip 0.36 %; right speaker [640,335,700,435] median 35.2

change.to: 170 W, cone 34 deg, aimed at the cabinet's upper edge so light rakes the acrylic and its polished edges

changes.expected: Cabinet faces and edges readable as smoked acrylic, batts no longer clipping, the pair the brightest coloured object at the far end.

changes.problem: The figures read as translucent untextured mannequins, the strongest 'render' cue in the frame.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x: smooth grey bodies, ghosted through by the record wall, no fabric or hair

change.from: shutter 1.0 frame; head travel [0.16, 0.09, 0.03] m, turn 30.0 deg
change.to: shutter 0.4 frame; head travel [0.06, 0.03, 0.01] m, turn 12 deg; only the bartender and the selector moving, the others nearly still (faces still unsharp)

changes.expected: Bodies mostly solid and dressed, with blur only on a moving head or hand, as a real 1/4 s exposure records seated people.

changes.problem: Mother EARF, the room's centrepiece, reads as a black wire cage, not thick smoked acrylic.

change.to: 120 W, cone 24 deg, so the 25 mm disc edges catch and pipe light and the wall shadow stays hard

changes.expected: Disc edges glow, the smoke reads translucent with depth through it, the shadow on the concrete becomes a crisp patterned shadow.

changes.problem: The zinc counter top reads as white marble or plastic and is the brightest large surface in the frame.

change.setting: the zinc's patina; the Domes' downlights
change.to: darker aged zinc (albedo about 40 % lower, roughness up, mottled patina); downlights 11 W

changes.expected: Counter reads as dull grey-warm zinc with pools under each Dome rather than a uniform white slab.

changes.problem: The foreground floor is bright, smooth grey and pulls the eye away from the room.

change.to: darker warm concrete, matte with low sheen and visible aggregate and wear

changes.expected: Foreground falls into shadow, leading the eye to the pools on the tables and to the altar.

changes.problem: The right-wall screens show near-blank grey-lilac fields that read as missing textures.

evidence.measured: lum_median 67.9, b_median 66 vs g 65 (cool cast against warm wall)

change.to: 0.012, so the image content reads as a dim print rather than a lit blank panel

changes.expected: Frames recede into the wall, warm-neutral, with their image legible in the shadows.

changes.problem: The back room is a flat dark band with no air between it and the front.
changes.expected: Faint beams in the altar and Dome spots, separation in depth, shadows lifted a little.

changes.problem: At 28 mm the altar pair is about 5 % of the frame width and the empty foreground floor takes the lower third.

evidence.measured: the pair spans about 200 px of 1200

change.to: lens 32 mm, target [16.5, 2.9, 1.3], still from the door

changes.expected: Altar larger and nearer the centre, less floor, the counter and banquette still framing both sides.
